records.subject: 29 Aug — Beheading of St John the Baptist (Class II)
records.title: Salome with the Head of Saint John the Baptist
records.rightsStatus: CMA object-specific Open Access, unrestricted reuse; official download available
records.summaryEn: Dutch oil on wood, mid-1600s, unframed 71 × 54.6 cm. The execution is already over; Salome and Herodias receive the Baptist's head. A strong vertical Baroque candidate, but not the actual moment of execution and not yet an approved calendar hero.
records.summaryFr: Huile sur bois néerlandaise du milieu du XVIIe siècle, 71 × 54,6 cm hors cadre. La décollation est déjà accomplie : Salomé et Hérodiade reçoivent la tête du Baptiste. Candidat baroque vertical, mais non la scène même de l'exécution et non approuvé pour le calendrier.
records.imageRoute: official CMA object page download; do not preserve ephemeral signed Piction thumbnail URL

records.subject: 29 Aug — Beheading of St John the Baptist (Class II)
records.title: Salome with the Head of Saint John the Baptist
records.rightsStatus: Object image Public Domain; Met Open Access CC0
records.summaryEn: Italian oil on wood c.1507–1509, 57.2 × 47 cm. The executioner's hand alone appears, presenting John's head to Salome. Exact physical object and unrestricted museum image route; subject is the aftermath, not the act of beheading.
records.summaryFr: Huile sur bois italienne vers 1507–1509, 57,2 × 47 cm. Seule la main du bourreau apparaît, présentant la tête de Jean à Salomé. Objet et voie d'image libre identifiés ; scène postérieure à l'exécution.
records.imageRouteNote: Official object page exposes this IIIF path; bytes not fetched in this pass

records.subject: 29 Aug — Beheading of St John the Baptist (Class II)
records.artist: Follower of Bernardino Luini (current main CMA attribution)
records.title: Salome with the Head of Saint John the Baptist
records.rightsStatus: CMA object-specific Open Access, unrestricted reuse; official download available
records.summaryEn: Oil on canvas, 1500s or later, unframed 46.6 × 59.7 cm. Dark horizontal composition with Salome, Herodias and the Baptist's head. The main institutional heading says follower of Bernardino Luini, although a lower page label says Bernardino Luini: retain follower attribution and flag internal display inconsistency.
records.summaryFr: Huile sur toile, XVIe siècle ou plus tard, 46,6 × 59,7 cm hors cadre. Composition sombre horizontale montrant Salomé, Hérodiade et la tête du Baptiste. La notice principale attribue l'œuvre à un suiveur de Bernardino Luini ; un libellé secondaire indique Luini lui-même. Conserver l'attribution prudente.
records.imageRoute: official CMA object page download; avoid ephemeral signed thumbnail

records.subject: 29 Aug — Beheading of St John the Baptist (Class II)
records.title: The Feast of Herod and the Beheading of the Baptist
records.rightsStatus: Object image Public Domain; Met Open Access CC0
records.summaryEn: A c.1330–1335 tempera, gold and silver panel, 44.1 × 49.8 cm, from a dispersed Baptist altarpiece. The Met identifies both Herod's feast and the martyrdom narrative. Strong literal subject but medieval rather than the preferred dark Baroque oil.
records.summaryFr: Panneau à tempera, or et argent, vers 1330–1335, 44,1 × 49,8 cm, issu d'un retable dispersé consacré au Baptiste. La notice du Met documente le banquet d'Hérode et la décollation. Sujet exact mais esthétique médiévale, non baroque.
records.medium: tempera on wood, gold ground and silver
records.imageRouteNote: Official object page exposed this IIIF route; bytes not acquired

records.subject: 22 Feb — Chair of St Peter (Class II)
records.title: Christ Giving the Keys of Heaven to Saint Peter
records.accession: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, Gemäldegalerie B.116; obj:863360
records.rightsStatus: Institutional 2022 Open Access initiative supports high-resolution free reproductions of public-domain works; exact downloadable file's license still to inspect
records.summaryEn: Oil on oak, dated by the custodian 1613/15, 182.5 × 159 cm. The museum connects the handing over of the keys with the papal office. Relevant to Matthew 16:13–19 in the Chair of Peter Mass but not a depiction of the historic Antioch cathedra. Download is exposed; image-specific license and native pixels remain unverified.
records.summaryFr: Huile sur chêne, datée 1613–1615 par le musée, 182,5 × 159 cm. La remise des clefs évoque la primauté de Pierre et Matthieu 16, mais non le siège historique d'Antioche. Téléchargement annoncé ; licence propre au fichier et pixels natifs non contrôlés.
records.imageRoute: official SMB object page Download; no unverified static image URL

records.subject: 22 Feb — Chair of St Peter (Class II)
records.artist: Anonymous artist, related to Peter Paul Rubens
records.title: Saint Peter
records.rightsStatus: NGA object-specific public domain free image
records.summaryEn: Oil on panel c.1616/1618, 92 × 67.5 cm, showing Peter holding two keys against a dark ground. NGA states the design derives from Rubens's Saint Philip in the Lerma series, NOT a personally painted Rubens Saint Peter. The Prado original is not an eligible image source. This is an apostle portrait, not the Chair scene.
records.summaryFr: Huile sur bois vers 1616–1618, 92 × 67,5 cm, saint Pierre portant deux clefs sur fond sombre. La NGA explique que le modèle reprend le saint Philippe de la série Lerma de Rubens ; l'œuvre n'est pas un portrait autographe de Rubens. L'original du Prado reste exclu. Portrait apparenté, non scène de la Chaire.

records.subject: 22 Feb — Chair of St Peter (Class II)
records.title: Christ Giving the Keys to Saint Peter
records.rightsStatus: NGA object-specific public domain free image
records.summaryEn: Tempera and gold leaf on vellum, c.1395–1400, 34.4 × 31.4 cm. Exact Matthew 16 keys scene, not a painting of the Chair itself. The NGA's 2008 attribution correction confirms Lorenzo Monaco rather than a generic Italian fifteenth-century painter. A secondary miniature, not a Baroque hero recommendation.
records.summaryFr: Miniature à tempera et or sur vélin, vers 1395–1400, 34,4 × 31,4 cm. Scène exacte de la remise des clefs selon Matthieu 16, non représentation de la Chaire. La NGA a confirmé l'attribution à Lorenzo Monaco en 2008. Illustration secondaire, non proposition de héros baroque.
records.medium: tempera and gold leaf on vellum

records.subject: 22 Feb — Chair of St Peter (Class II)
records.title: The Sacrament of Ordination (Christ Presenting the Keys to Saint Peter)
records.accession: Kimbell Art Museum, collection route ap-201101
records.rightsStatus: Official object and oil identity verified; freely reusable exact photograph NOT verified
records.summaryEn: Poussin's c.1636–1640 oil on canvas, 95.9 × 121.6 cm, shows Christ entrusting keys to Peter. An exact physical painting and compelling Matthew 16 link, but the Kimbell page did not establish a no-fee commercial-use image licence; do not infer one from the age of the painting.
records.summaryFr: Huile sur toile de Poussin vers 1636–1640, 95,9 × 121,6 cm, représentant la remise des clefs. L'objet physique et son rapport à Matthieu 16 sont identifiés, mais la réutilisation commerciale gratuite de la photographie n'est pas établie ; conserver le blocage.

records.subject: 7 Oct — Our Lady of the Rosary (Class II)
records.title: The Madonna of the Rosary
records.rightsStatus: NGA object-specific public domain free image
records.summaryEn: Signed and dated 1674 pen-and-ink drawing, 32.3 × 24 cm, with Madonna, Child, cherubs and rosary beads. Exact devotional subject with free image route, but a drawing rather than the requested high-impact oil hero. Keep for supporting illustration only.
records.summaryFr: Dessin à la plume signé et daté 1674, 32,3 × 24 cm, montrant la Vierge, l'Enfant, des chérubins et des chapelets. Sujet dévotionnel exact et image libre, mais dessin secondaire plutôt que peinture à l'huile héroïque.
records.medium: pen and brown ink on laid paper

records.subject: 7 Oct — Our Lady of the Rosary (Class II)
records.title: Madonna of the Rosary
records.rightsStatus: KHM object page displays Copyright Kunsthistorisches Museum, Gemäldegalerie; independent freely reusable exact photograph not established
records.summaryEn: The custodian identifies the oil painting as c.1603, 364.5 × 249.5 cm, showing Saint Dominic distributing rosaries. A third-party site calls the reproduction CC0, but that cannot override the museum's explicit image copyright statement. Do not acquire or publish an image based only on the aggregator claim.
records.summaryFr: Le musée attribue cette huile à Caravage, vers 1603, 364,5 × 249,5 cm ; saint Dominique y distribue des chapelets. Une plateforme tierce qualifie la reproduction de CC0, mais la notice du dépositaire indique explicitement un copyright. Ne pas publier sur cette seule base.
